column1: # testdata/wire/skipped-value — a value a reader SKIPS is held to what a read
# of it would hold, in every form (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §4, §16.3;
# docs/rulings.json skipped-value-is-validated).
# Two units under test/skipped-value/: reader/Reader.schema declares `known`
# only; writer/Writer.schema declares `known` plus one extra field of each shape
# the reader does not — a string, a float, a quantized float, a counted array,
# an enum-keyed array and a nested table. A reader of the reader unit skips each
# extra field and is held to what a read of it would hold, in the JSON and the
# message form.
# Columns, tab-separated: file, form (json or message), verdict (read or refused).
# JSON rows read at the reader unit's Root. Message rows decode a batch of one
# Root body against announcement.bin (the writer unit's announcement): the
# canonical batch reads, and each damaged batch refuses, one per message-skip
# condition of docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.3 that this writer unit can carry. Three
# conditions have no batch: a nested body naming a reserved id needs a
# vocabulary no conforming writer announces; a ranged integer's offset over the
# sender's max needs a ranged integer, and the writer unit declares none; and a
# keyed array's count out of [min, max] cannot be written, since the [Color]
# count's two bits hold 0 to 3 and every one of those is within its bounds.
